note: Invented UK small businesses, none a client. Briefs say who, where and what they do, nothing about how to write. Genres are the prompts; {brief} is replaced. The two email genres match the register of the Enron baseline, so a feature that only separates marketing from email is caught.

genres.service-blurb: Write the short description of the main service, two to four sentences, for the website of {brief} Reply with the text only.
genres.booking-description: Write the description shown on the booking page for a first appointment or consultation with {brief} Two to four sentences. Reply with the text only.
genres.cta-block: Write the text for the closing call-to-action section of the home page for {brief} One heading line, then one to three sentences. Reply with the text only.
genres.enquiry-reply: You run {brief} A customer has emailed asking whether you can help them and roughly what it would cost. Write your reply. Body only, no subject line.
genres.internal-email: You work at {brief} Write a short email to a colleague about moving two of next week's jobs to different days. Body only, no subject line.

edit:
Edit this to sound more human. Reply with the edited text only.
